payingUser: A choir, band, orchestra or piano student who photographs borrowed or marked-up paper scores and needs a clean rehearsal copy that can leave the phone.
paidUnit: A paid, no-ad app that turns a batch of score photographs into a cropped, deskewed, ordered and shareable rehearsal PDF without a renewal.
momentOfPayment: The one-time purchase is taken when the user exports the first multi-page rehearsal PDF after reviewing the enhanced pages.
distinctnessSentence: Scorefolio makes a print-ready rehearsal PDF from a batch of photographed music pages with manual page ordering, score-specific crop and deskew review, and Android share/export, instead of attempting error-prone note recognition or trapping one scanned page behind recurring limits.
day1RevenuePath: The listing meets the measured sheet music scanner query, where the paid $19.99 Sheet Music Scanner & Reader has 50K+ installs and the 50K+ and 100K+ weak mid-tier apps draw paywall and broken-scan complaints; the first export is the single, visible value moment for the $9.99 unlock.
assumptionsUnverified: The $9.99 price is inferred from the measured $19.99 paid incumbent, not from this developer account's conversion data.
Play install buckets are rounded and the review sample contains only three reviews per app page, so neither market size nor complaint frequency is measured exactly.
No trademark-register search has tested Scorefolio in class 9, and a clean visible Play-title reading would not establish clearance.
The app must prove that Android image processing produces sufficiently legible music notation across real lighting and paper conditions; the market scan does not test image quality.
